name: London
hook: The city of the Great Fire, the Blitz and Jack the Ripper.

facts.label: the Great Fire
facts.statement: The Great Fire of 1666 burned much of London; in 1986 a bakers' union formally apologized for starting it.

facts.label: Westminster Abbey
facts.statement: Westminster Abbey, formally the Collegiate Church of St. Peter, holds Britain's Unknown Soldier in the only floor tomb visitors may not walk on.

facts.label: Jack the Ripper
facts.statement: Jack the Ripper killed in London's Whitechapel district in 1888; his victims included Elizabeth Stride and Catherine Eddowes.

facts.label: Buckingham Palace
facts.statement: Buckingham Palace, the royal London residence, has 600 rooms and was bombed during the Blitz on September 13, 1940.

facts.label: the British Museum
facts.statement: The British Museum houses the Rosetta Stone and, thanks to Norman Foster, a glass-enclosed courtyard.

facts.label: St. Paul's Cathedral
facts.statement: St. Paul's Cathedral, Christopher Wren's seat of the Bishop of London, had its bells cast at Whitechapel's foundry.

facts.label: Hyde Park
facts.statement: Hyde Park, a former royal hunting preserve, hosted the 1851 Great Exhibition in the Crystal Palace and is home to Speakers' Corner.
